title: Usage guide
text: toml_parse() reads TOML text; toml_read() reads file, URL connection. return named list, keys order document gives .
code: doc <- ' title = "Example"  [server] host = "localhost" port = 8080 tags = ["web", "api"]  [[users]] name = "ana" admin = true  [[users]] name = "bo" ' x <- toml_parse(doc) str(x) #> List of 3 #>  $ title : chr "Example" #>  $ server:List of 3 #>   ..$ host: chr "localhost" #>   ..$ port: int 8080 #>   ..$ tags: chr [1:2] "web" "api" #>  $ users :List of 2 #>   ..$ :List of 2 #>   .. ..$ name : chr "ana" #>   .. ..$ admin: logi TRUE #>   ..$ :List of 1 #>   .. ..$ name: chr "bo" path <- tempfile(fileext = ".toml") writeLines(doc, path) toml_read(path)$server$port #> [1] 8080

title: Usage guide
text: select returns value path, written TOML key syntax: dots keys, quotes around keys need , [] array elements, counting 1. whole document still checked, since TOML lets table added anywhere , selected part becomes R values. path document error, never NULL:
code: toml_parse(doc, select = "server") #> $host #> [1] "localhost" #>  #> $port #> [1] 8080 #>  #> $tags #> [1] "web" "api" toml_parse(doc, select = "users[2].name") #> [1] "bo" toml_read(path, select = c("server", "tags")) #> [1] "web" "api" try(toml_parse(doc, select = "server.timeout")) #> Error : TOML document has no `server.timeout`: `server` has no `timeout`

str(toml_parse("a = [1, 2]
b = [1, 2.5]
c = [true, 1]
d = []
e = [3]")) #> List of 5 #>  $ a: int [1:2] 1 2 #>  $ b: num [1:2] 1 2.5 #>  $ c:List of 2 #>   ..$ : logi TRUE #>   ..$ : int 1 #>  $ d: logi(0)  #>  $ e: 'AsIs' int 3

title: Usage guide
text: toml_emit() writes named list TOML text; toml_write() writes file connection. table’s values come first, sub-tables, TOML requires. port = 8080 double R written integer TOML reader expects; non-whole doubles written shortest digits read back exactly. list named lists, data frame, becomes array tables. output every platform, reads back: NA NULL TOML form, refused unless na = "omit". Arrays past width characters written one element per line, inline = n writes small flat tables inline.
code: cfg <- list(   title = "Example",   port = 8080,   ratio = 0.75,   started = as.Date("2026-10-08"),   server = list(host = "localhost", tags = c("web", "api")),   users = list(list(name = "ana"), list(name = "bo")) ) cat(toml_emit(cfg)) #> title = "Example" #> port = 8080 #> ratio = 0.75 #> started = 2026-10-08 #>  #> [server] #> host = "localhost" #> tags = ["web", "api"] #>  #> [[users]] #> name = "ana" #>  #> [[users]] #> name = "bo" identical(toml_parse(toml_emit(cfg))$users, cfg$users) #> [1] TRUE

what: Choose how one value is written
title: Usage guide
text: Markers change value written, never reads back : toml_inline() writes table inline, toml_literal() writes literal strings need escapes, toml_multiline() writes multi-line strings.
code: cat(toml_emit(list(   dependencies = list(     serde = toml_inline(list(version = "1.0", features = "derive")),     rand = "0.8"   ),   pattern = toml_literal("^\\d+\\.\\d+$"),   motd = toml_multiline("Welcome!") ))) #> pattern = '^\d+\.\d+$' #> motd = """ #> Welcome!""" #>  #> [dependencies] #> serde = { version = "1.0", features = "derive" } #> rand = "0.8"

title: Usage guide
text: positions = TRUE records every key array element defined, check configuration can say problem : path column uses syntax select.
code:
cfg <- toml_parse("[server]
host = 'localhost'
port = 99999
", positions = TRUE) pos <- attr(cfg, "toml_positions") pos #>          path    type line column offset #> 1      server   table    1      2      1 #> 2 server.host  string    2      1      9 #> 3 server.port integer    3      1     28 at <- pos[pos$path == "server.port", ] sprintf("server.port (line %d, column %d) must be at most 65535", at$line, at$column) #> [1] "server.port (line 3, column 1) must be at most 65535"

title: Usage guide
text: toml_validate() runs whole check without building R value. returns TRUE FALSE, error = TRUE raises reason:
code:
toml_validate("a = 1
b = 2") #> [1] TRUE toml_validate("a = 1
a = 2") #> [1] FALSE try(toml_validate("a = 1
a = 2", error = TRUE)) #> Error : TOML parse error at line 2, column 1: key defined twice

[t]
"), zutoml_parse_error = function(e) e) c(err$kind, err$line, err$column) #> [1] "table_redefined" "3"               "2"

title: Usage guide
text: zutoml reads TOML 1.1.0 default, adds \e \xHH escapes, times without seconds, newlines trailing commas inline tables. version = "1.0.0" reads strictly. emitter always writes text TOML 1.0.0 readers accept.

Types come document. 2024-01-01 Date; "2024-01-01" string. zutoml never guesses string’s content. Strict. invalid document refused, line column fault condition class can catch. Size, depth, item string limits bound untrusted input. Deterministic output. R value gives bytes every platform, text reads back.

title: Parse a TOML document — toml_parse
code: toml_parse(   x,   select = NULL,   version = c("1.1.0", "1.0.0"),   simplify = c("preserve", "none"),   data_frame = FALSE,   big_integers = c("bigint", "double", "error"),   datetimes = c("convert", "keep"),   local_time = c("character", "difftime"),   positions = FALSE,   max_size = 64 * 1024^2,   max_depth = 128L,   max_items = 1e+06,   max_string = 2^31 - 1 )

title: Parse a TOML document — toml_parse
text: x TOML document: single string, raw vector UTF-8 bytes. select NULL (default) returns whole document. path returns value : string TOML key syntax, positions table writes ("tool.poetry"; '".b".c' key dot; "products[2].name" arrays, counting 1), vector two keys taken (c("tool", "poetry")). whole document still read checked, since TOML lets table added anywhere , selected part becomes R values. path document raises zutoml_missing_key, path found, part path exist. version TOML version read: "1.1.0" (default) "1.0.0", refuses forms 1.1.0 added (\e \xHH escapes, times without seconds, newlines trailing comma inline tables). simplify "preserve" (default) turns arrays whose elements share type vectors; "none" makes every array list. data_frame TRUE, array whose elements tables becomes data frame: one row per table, columns first-seen key order, missing keys NA. Columns whose values share type lists. getOption("zutoml.max_df_cells", 1e7) cells raises zutoml_limit_error, since rows share keys make frame quadratic size. big_integers integers beyond 2^53, double hold exactly: "bigint" (default) returns toml_bigint() vector exact decimal text; "double" nearest double; "error" raises zutoml_unrepresentable. datetimes "convert" (default) returns POSIXct Date; "keep" returns date-times text. local_time "character" (default) returns local time text; "difftime" seconds since midnight. positions TRUE, result carries attribute "toml_positions": data frame one row per key array element, order parsed value, giving path TOML key syntax (servers[2].ip, keys quoted TOML needs , array elements numbered 1), type ("table", "inline_table", "array_of_tables", "array", "string", "integer", "float", "bool", "datetime", "datetime-local", "date-local" "time-local"), line, column (1-based, characters) byte offset (0-based) defined: key's position keyed value, [[header]] table array tables. Code checks configuration can say value wrong. max_size largest document accepted, bytes, Inf. max_depth deepest nesting tables arrays, counting ; 1023. max_items keys plus array elements, Inf. max_string longest string key, decoded bytes, Inf.

title: Parse a TOML document — toml_parse
text: named list, one element per top-level key; select, value path.

title: Parse a TOML document — toml_parse
text: array becomes vector elements strings, booleans, numbers, dates, date-times one kind. Numbers widen: integers floats give double vector. Booleans never join numbers. empty array logical(0). one-element array becomes vector marked (), writing back gives array . Anything else list. simplify = "none" makes every array list. datetimes = "keep", date-times returned RFC 3339 text instead ("1979-05-27T07:32:00Z", zero offset written Z, fraction 0, 3, 6 9 digits). Fractions past nanoseconds truncated, TOML requires; POSIXct holds microseconds. Valid TOML R hold raises zutoml_unrepresentable: string key containing U+0000, float beyond range double, integer beyond 2^53 big_integers = "error".

title: Parse a TOML document — toml_parse
code: doc <- ' title = "TOML Example" ports = [8000, 8001, 8002]  [owner] name = "Tom Preston-Werner" dob = 1979-05-27T07:32:00-08:00  [[products]] name = "Hammer" sku = 738594937  [[products]] name = "Nail" sku = 284758393 color = "gray" ' x <- toml_parse(doc) x$owner$dob #> [1] "1979-05-27 15:32:00 UTC" x$ports #> [1] 8000 8001 8002  toml_parse(doc, data_frame = TRUE)$products #>     name       sku color #> 1 Hammer 738594937  <NA> #> 2   Nail 284758393  gray  # Only part of it: toml_parse(doc, select = "owner") #> $name #> [1] "Tom Preston-Werner" #>  #> $dob #> [1] "1979-05-27 15:32:00 UTC" #>  toml_parse(doc, select = "products[2].color") #> [1] "gray"  # Where each value is, for messages about the document: pos <- attr(toml_parse(doc, positions = TRUE), "toml_positions") pos[pos$path == "owner.dob", ] #>        path     type line column offset #> 8 owner.dob datetime    7      1     88

what: zutoml: Read and Write 'TOML' Documents — zutoml-package
title: zutoml: Read and Write 'TOML' Documents — zutoml-package
text: Parses 'TOML' (Tom's Obvious Minimal Language) documents, versions 1.0.0 1.1.0 https://toml.io/en/v1.1.0, ordinary R values, writes R values 'TOML'. Every 'TOML' type maps one R type, including four date time types, strings never reinterpreted. Invalid documents refused line column fault, configurable size, depth, item string limits, output deterministic. directions pass 'toml-test' conformance suite https://github.com/toml-lang/toml-test. parser writer written C, system library required.

title: zutoml 0.1.0
text: Initial CRAN submission. toml_read() reads TOML document file, URL connection, never holding max_size + 1 bytes. toml_parse() reads TOML document ordinary R values: tables named lists document order, arrays vectors elements share type, date-times POSIXct Date, integers beyond 2^53 toml_bigint(). data_frame = TRUE turns arrays tables data frames. toml_emit() toml_write() write named list TOML: deterministic text, tables [headers], lists tables data frames arrays tables, errors name key path value fault. toml_parse(select = "tool.poetry"), toml_read(), returns value path, building R values rest document; path document raises zutoml_missing_key. toml_parse(positions = TRUE) records every key array element defined (path, type, line, column, offset), code checks configuration can point value fault. toml_inline(), toml_literal() toml_multiline() mark one value written toml_emit(). toml_validate() checks document valid TOML, within size, depth, item string limits, error = TRUE says (line, column, offset kind classed condition). zutoml_info() reports versions zutoml built toml-test suite passes. Every case toml-test suite passes, TOML 1.0.0 1.1.0, directions. TOML 1.1.0 read default; version = "1.0.0" reads strictly; emitter always writes TOML 1.0.0. vignette, vignette("zutoml"), reads pyproject.toml Cargo.toml writes configuration.
